claim: vLLM v0.6.0 achieves 2.7x higher throughput and 5x faster time-per-output-token than v0.5.3 for Llama 3 8B, and 1.8x higher throughput / 2x lower TPOT for Llama 3 70B.
scope_conditions: Measured on 1xH100 (8B) and 4xH100 (70B) using ShareGPT dataset, 500 prompts, TPOT measured at 32 QPS; comparison is version-to-version (v0.5.3 vs v0.6.0), not an absolute tokens/sec figure
quoted_support: vLLM achieves 2.7x higher throughput and 5x faster TPOT (time per output token) on Llama 8B model, and 1.8x higher throughput and 2x less TPOT on Llama 70B model.

claim: Under light load, Llama 3 8B generates one output token roughly every 13ms, implying a single-stream decode rate near 77 tokens/sec.
stance_target: concrete per-token latency baseline for ~7-8B models under vLLM
scope_conditions: Single request, light load (not batched), H100 GPU, used to motivate API-server streaming-object-rate discussion, not a batched-generation figure
quoted_support: Llama3 8B can generate 1 token every 13 ms under light load. This translates to the frontend needing to stream back 76 objects per second

claim: vLLM's official Llama-3-8B-on-1xA100 benchmark appendix exists but the concrete tokens/sec throughput values are only presented as chart images, not as extractable text, in this blog post.
stance_target: availability of concrete A100 batched-throughput numbers for 7-8B models
scope_conditions: Applies specifically to the 'Llama 3 8B on 1xA100' and 'Llama 3 70B on 4xA100' appendix sections of this post
quoted_support: On Llama 3 8B, vLLM achieves comparable TTFT and TPOT on ShareGPT and decode-heavy dataset as TensorRT-LLM and SGLang. ... Throughput-wise, TensorRT-LLM has the highest throughput among all engines, and vLLM has the second highest throughput on ShareGPT and decode-heavy dataset.

claim: The benchmark workloads used to characterize vLLM throughput have short-to-moderate sequence lengths: ShareGPT averages 202 input/179 output tokens; a prefill-heavy synthetic set averages 462 input/16 output tokens; a decode-heavy synthetic set averages 462 input/256 output tokens.
scope_conditions: 500 prompts per dataset, fixed random seed, applies to vLLM v0.6.0 benchmark methodology
quoted_support: Prefill-heavy dataset: 500 prompts synthetically generated from sonnet dataset with roughly 462 input tokens and 16 output tokens on average. Decode-heavy dataset: ... roughly the same amount of 462 input tokens and 256 output tokens on average.

claim: Multi-step scheduling (batching multiple decode steps before returning to the CPU scheduler) improved Llama 70B throughput on 4xH100 by 28%, and asynchronous output processing improved TPOT by 8.7% for the same setup.
stance_target: sources of vLLM throughput gains, relevant to whether A100 throughput would benefit similarly
quoted_support: This improves the throughput of running Llama 70B models on 4xH100 by 28%. ... This improves the time-per-output-token of running Llama 70B models on 4xH100 by 8.7%.
